note: Real Earth-observation satellites for the "your design resembles…" match. Figures are approximate (launch mass, typical power, mean altitude), from memory of public agency pages, not checked line by line. Summaries are our own words.

missions.name: Landsat 8
missions.summary: Images the whole Earth every 16 days in visible, infrared and thermal bands; used to map burn scars and land change.

missions.name: Landsat 9
missions.summary: Flies 8 days apart from Landsat 8, so together they revisit every place every 8 days.

missions.name: Terra
missions.summary: Its MODIS instrument sees the whole Earth every 1–2 days and has detected active fires every morning for over 20 years.

missions.name: Aqua
missions.summary: Terra's afternoon partner, also with MODIS; together they give two fire observations per day.

missions.name: Suomi NPP
missions.summary: Its VIIRS instrument has a 3,000 km wide swath and spots small fires day and night.

missions.name: NOAA-20 (JPSS-1)
missions.summary: A weather satellite carrying VIIRS, flying half an orbit apart from Suomi NPP for more frequent fire views.

missions.name: GOES-16
missions.summary: Stays above one spot on the equator and images the Americas every few minutes, so it sees fires start, but with coarse pixels.

missions.name: Sentinel-2A
missions.summary: Sharp 10 m colour and infrared images with a 290 km swath; used to map burned areas after fires.

missions.name: Sentinel-3A
missions.summary: Measures surface temperature with a wide thermal instrument that also produces a nightly fire product.

missions.name: BIRD
missions.summary: A small satellite built to show that infrared cameras on a 100 kg spacecraft can detect and measure wildfires.

missions.name: TET-1 (FireBIRD)
missions.summary: A technology-test small satellite that carried BIRD's fire cameras again, as part of a two-satellite fire mission.

missions.name: FOREST-2
missions.summary: A commercial CubeSat with a thermal camera, an early step towards a wildfire-monitoring constellation.

missions.name: Planet Dove (Flock)
missions.summary: 3U CubeSats with 3–5 m colour cameras; hundreds of them together image most land every day and show smoke plumes.

missions.name: ECOSTRESS (on the ISS)
missions.summary: A thermal instrument on the Space Station; its tilted orbit passes at different times of day and catches fire heat at night.

sources.source: NASA, NOAA, ESA and DLR mission pages (approximate, not checked line by line)
sources.note: Rounded figures for matching only; ECOSTRESS mass and power are for the instrument, not the ISS.
